notes: Acceptance structure and scenarios frozen ahead of execution; capability scope is still under semantic review (SP003 matrix work in progress), so not all capabilities are frozen.
No row here claims live verification that has not already been recorded elsewhere; recorded_evidence rows only reference existing files.

bounded.max_requests / max_operations are null and freeze_required=true wherever no executed tool or explicit authorization defines a bound; no values are invented for unknown devices, accounts, or counts.

result distinguishes recorded_evidence (an existing evidence file) from awaiting_resource_confirmation, awaiting_authorization, awaiting_design, blocked, and pending_execution; blocked is never counted as passed. resource_state qualifies resource readiness (e.g. user_confirmed_no_bound_device, unknown_awaiting_configuration_check) and never marks a row complete.

The domestic sync row's 7-request bound and 6-business-logical-call count come from tools/live/verify_diagnostics.py (the executor of the 2026-11-16-diagnostics-v1 receipt): devices.list plus the inspect_device five (get/channels/status/capabilities/version) = 6 business logical entries, plus one auth HTTP call = 7 total; verify_devices.py is not the executor of that receipt.
No tokens, serials, raw business responses, or account/device identifiers appear in this file.

cases.capability_selector: platform message push (inbound webhook verify/parse/ack semantics)
cases.account_role_permissions: service-enabled account with message push configured and an independent secret
cases.device_requirements: a target type whose events generate real platform messages
preconditions: message push service enabled for the account
reachable callback endpoint under test control
independent secret for signature verification
authorization to trigger a real message of the target type
dedup and platform redelivery semantics defined before execution (which header/field is the dedup key, how redelivery is distinguished from a new message)

authorization covering documented configuration side effects: enabling/modifying the message service takes ~2h to take effect, stops the same-phone-number EZVIZ App device-message reminders, and disabling the service does not auto-restore them (customer-service/ticket required); console 'message test' suspends the original callback and temporarily opens all message types — the prior read-only scope does not cover these operations

expected_evidence.read: real callback received at the controlled endpoint; signature verified over the raw body/headers exactly as delivered (not over re-serialized JSON); the correct ACK contract actually returned to the platform per the source (success=HTTP 200 plus body containing messageId); observed behavior for at least one platform duplicate/redelivery of the same message and how it was classified; observed timeout or non-2xx handling on at least one controlled failure path; error-path handling verified (bad signature rejected, malformed body rejected, unexpected type tolerated); replay boundary explicitly demonstrated (an out-of-window or previously-acked message is not treated as a fresh accepted message). Domestic header 't' timestamp is confirmed as milliseconds (5130); overseas 't' unit, freshness window, timeout/limits (2s vs 'usually 3 tries / ~5s' conflict) and ciphertext wording conflicts remain unconfirmed pending configuration review; none of the unconfirmed values are invented here.

cases.recovery_plan: callback endpoint torn down; secret rotated if exposed
blockers: Pure-function helpers and synthetic vectors do not substitute for platform real callbacks; signature freshness, duplicate delivery semantics, timeout, and ciphertext semantics remain open questions per the source review. Service, endpoint, secret, target type, and trigger authorization are all unconfirmed; user stated on 2026-11-17 they do not know the platform message service or which callback entry is usable, so the exact service/configuration state is unknown_awaiting_configuration_check. Configuration side effects (App reminder suppression, ~2h effective delay, console test temporarily suspending the original callback and opening all types) require explicit authorization beyond the prior read-only scope. A single successful callback alone does not close this required row.

release_gates.item: product prerequisite: scope/capability matrix reviewed and ratified (no source row left unreviewed); every matrix capability has a recorded disposition
release_gates.notes: needs_review, blocked_source, and unratified items are not admissible evidence and cannot be silently excluded or counted as complete; each must be resolved to a concrete disposition (implement / reuse_official_component / not_an_api / duplicate / deprecated / phase_2) with evidence before release. Engineering checks passing does not satisfy this gate.

release_gates.item: product prerequisite: every required-tier acceptance row implemented, documented, and acceptance-completed per its own criteria; example/CLI required rows exercised; required source-semantic issues dispositioned
release_gates.notes: all required rows must reach recorded_evidence (or an explicitly justified not_applicable disposition), not merely pending_execution/awaiting_*; needs_review/blocked_source/unratified required rows mean the gate fails. The pre-gates are an AND condition with the engineering gates below — green Ruff/mypy/pytest/audit alone does not permit upload.
current pyproject declares 0.1.0a1; the plan states the release version must be proposed after scope/compatibility are fixed, not assumed already published
